title: Caregiver integration during discharge planning of older adults
text: The meta-analysis found lower readmission when caregivers were integrated into discharge planning: RR 0.75 (95% CI 0.62 to 0.91) at 90 days and RR 0.76 (0.64 to 0.90) at 180 days. This is evidence for a discharge-planning intervention, not evidence for the probability of routing to community care or the time required to process a discharge letter.

title: Admission avoidance hospital at home
text: Across 20 randomised trials with 3,100 participants, hospital at home had mortality RR 0.88 (95% CI 0.68 to 1.13), readmission RR 1.14 (0.97 to 1.34), and residential-care RR 0.53 (0.41 to 0.69) in older populations. Hospital length of stay ranged from 4.1 to 18.5 days for hospital care and 1.2 to 5.1 days for the hospital-at-home groups; total hospital-at-home treatment ranged from 3 to 20.7 days. These estimates apply to selected patients receiving a staffed clinical service, not to an arbitrary increase in community routing. Eligibility, escalation and programme capacity must be represented before applying an outcome effect.

title: Measuring quality in community nursing: a mixed-methods study
text: Observed community-nursing visits ranged from 5 to 95 minutes. Average visits were 35 minutes for senior or specialist community nurses and 23 minutes for band 5 district nurses. The observed range is genuine but combines heterogeneous visit purposes and staff grades. It should inform sensitivity or validation, not silently replace NHS-SIM's documented constant 90-minute generic community visit.

title: Standardising community health services to address variation
text: The guidance reports substantial unwarranted variation across community services, including an example of roughly five-fold staffing variation between services. This demonstrates that a single national point estimate is unsafe. It does not reveal the local site's slot capacity or visit duration, so use it to widen sensitivity analysis rather than as a direct calibration.

title: Core20PLUS5 for adults
text: Core20PLUS5 defines a population-health approach centred on the most deprived 20% of the national population, locally selected PLUS groups and five clinical areas requiring accelerated improvement. This is a stratification and equity framework, not an effect-size source. Use it to require subgroup reporting and avoid assuming an average benefit is equally distributed.

title: Workforce standards for the district nursing service
text: The workforce standards use 9 to 10 visits per day as a planning range and state that a scheduled visit should allow at least 30 minutes, excluding travel. These are professional planning standards for district nursing, not measured throughput for every community-care pathway. Travel, acuity and skill mix remain material.

title: Next steps for integrating primary care: Fuller stocktake
text: The stocktake proposes integrated neighbourhood teams, streamlined urgent same-day access and more personalised continuity for people with complex needs. It describes multidisciplinary routing across primary, community, mental-health, pharmacy and voluntary services. The document supports the available policy pathways but does not estimate referral probabilities. It must not be used to fill the routing fields numerically.

title: Variation in general-practice consultation length
text: Across 836 consultations, mean consultation duration varied from 5.7 to 8.5 minutes between practices and from 4.4 to 11 minutes between individual GPs. This is old observational UK evidence and consultation modes have changed. It is still a defensible broad range when the local simulator provides no GP consultation-time observation, but should be superseded by newer matched data.

title: Identifying how GPs spend their time and the obstacles they face
text: A time-and-motion study covering 7,679 GP tasks and 238 hours across 61 clinical sessions estimated operational failures at 5.0% of tasks (95% CI 4.5% to 5.4%) and 3.9% of clinical time (95% CI 3.2% to 4.5%). Operational-failure time is not equivalent to all GP administration. Use this interval for a waste or recoverable-capacity scenario, not as gpAdminShare itself.

title: Trends in clinical workload in UK primary care, 2005 to 2019
text: Age-standardised GP administrative workload rose from 4.60 minutes per person-year in 2005 to 12.53 in 2019, while total GP workload rose from 28.31 to 42.36 minutes. Dividing administrative by total GP workload gives observed shares of approximately 16.3% and 29.6%. The 16.3% to 29.6% range is a transparent derivation across two historical years, not a confidence interval or a cross-practice distribution. It is suitable as a broad literature prior for gpAdminShare, with this limitation visible.

title: Hospital discharge and community support guidance
text: The statutory guidance structures discharge around Home First and pathways 0 to 3, from no formal post-discharge support through increasingly intensive home, bed-based and long-term support. It describes transfer-of-care hubs coordinating health, social care, housing and voluntary-sector input. Pathway numbers are categories, not probabilities. This source defines valid discharge mechanisms but does not supply the share of people suitable for community routing in the simulator.

title: Workforce and patient safety: electronic communications at discharge
text: The July 2025 investigation describes patient-safety risks when discharge information is incomplete, delayed, sent to the wrong destination or difficult for primary-care staff to process. It treats electronic discharge communication as a cross-organisational workflow rather than a single transmission event. The investigation is highly relevant to failure modes but does not provide a transferable transition probability for the synthetic world. Keep the measured NHS-SIM letter-routing values as the direct calibration.

title: Neighbourhood health framework
text: The framework describes population-health management, integrated neighbourhood teams and outcome-oriented commissioning as the operating model for shifting care closer to home. Use it to constrain plausible policy mechanisms and governance, not to populate a numerical parameter.

title: Neighbourhood health guidelines 2025/26
text: The guidance links neighbourhood services with integrated intermediate care, Home First, step-up and step-down care, urgent neighbourhood services and community diagnostic capacity. It notes a national footprint of 170 community diagnostic centres by March 2025. This is service-design evidence. It names mechanisms available to a policy but does not quantify a transfer probability or patient-level effect.

title: NHS Oversight Framework 2025/26: urgent community response metric
text: The oversight metric defines performance as qualifying two-hour urgent community response referrals responded to within 2 hours divided by all qualifying referrals in the reporting period. Use this definition to label and calculate an output consistently. It supplies neither a capacity value nor a causal effect.

title: Delivering more joined-up care for local communities
text: The analysis reports 29,364 full-time-equivalent GPs in September 2015 and 27,200 in May 2023, a reduction of 2,164, alongside community workforce shortages and rising demand. This historical national workforce change shows capacity pressure but does not convert directly into sessions or slots for one synthetic site. Use it as scenario context, not local calibration.

title: NHS-SIM live-world calibration findings
text: The 12 September 2026 snapshot observed 1,312 attendances across 9 simulated days, implying approximately 142 arrivals per simulated day with a 140 to 144 sensitivity band. It also observed 6 GP sessions per day, 15 usable slots per session, 4 community slots and 8 staffed spaces. This is the best direct calibration source for the current synthetic world. The snapshot was gridlocked: 1,307 of 1,312 attendances remained waiting, so it cannot identify service throughput or stable queueing performance.

title: NHS-SIM Handbook
text: The local verification notes retain the handbook's stated workflow timings and API semantics used by the simulator. Community visits are documented as 90 minutes and discharge-document transitions as 60 minutes per hop. Use these values only for the synthetic NHS-SIM world. They are documented simulator mechanics, not estimates of real NHS performance and they supply no uncertainty range.

title: NICE NG27 evidence: transition from hospital to community
text: The evidence review reports that early discharge planning reduced readmission, with a risk ratio of 0.78 and 95% confidence interval 0.69 to 0.90 in the cited synthesis. This is an intervention effect on readmission, not the fraction routed to community care and not a document-processing time. It can parameterise a separately modelled discharge-planning effect only.

title: Remote vital-sign monitoring in admission-avoidance hospital at home
text: A systematic review of 21 randomised trials with 3,459 participants found mortality RR 0.94 (95% CI 0.78 to 1.12), readmission RR 1.02 (0.77 to 1.35), and length-of-stay mean difference 1.91 days (0.71 to 3.12) for hospital at home compared with hospital care. Reporting was insufficient to classify the monitoring approach in most studies; the automated-monitoring subgroup had readmission RR 0.30 (0.11 to 0.86). The overall intervals include little or no effect and the favourable automated subgroup is based on limited evidence. This is useful counterevidence to an automatic monitoring benefit, but it does not estimate a dose-response for monitoring frequency or a patient-routing probability.

title: Remote patient monitoring and healthcare utilisation in noncommunicable disease
text: A review of 40 randomised trials found a hospitalisation risk ratio of 0.86 (95% CI 0.77 to 0.95; low certainty; I-squared 55%). Across 12 studies, hospital stay was 0.84 days shorter (95% CI 0.06 to 1.61 days shorter; low certainty). The effect compares remote-monitoring programmes with usual care; it does not estimate a linear response to observation frequency. Treat it as a scenario-level effect distribution, not a direct monitoringIntensity multiplier.

title: 10 Year Health Plan, chapter 2: hospital to community
text: Chapter 2 commits to a Neighbourhood Health Service, care planning for people with complex needs, neighbourhood centres operating at least 12 hours a day on 6 days a week, and at least doubling personal health budgets by 2028 to 2029. These are national policy commitments and operating-model directions, not effect estimates. They justify policy scenarios but do not identify a numerical community-capacity multiplier or hospital-to-community routing share.

title: 10 Year Health Plan, chapter 3: analogue to digital
text: The plan says that by 2028 patients should be able to communicate with care professionals, view and draft care plans, and book or hold appointments through the NHS App. It also estimates that saving 90 seconds per GP appointment could release more than 2,000 full-time-equivalent staff capacity. The 90-second claim is a productivity illustration, not a measured consultation-time distribution. The chapter supports digital-access scenarios but does not set a telephone follow-up share or monitoring effect.

title: 10 Year Health Plan, chapter 6: transparency of quality
text: Chapter 6 commits to greater publication of quality measures and more systematic, comparable collection of patient-reported outcome measures and patient-reported experience measures. This source helps define reportable outcomes and auditability. It does not provide a model input or a numerical causal effect.

title: 10 Year Health Plan, chapter 8: innovation
text: Chapter 8 identifies advanced wearables and biomarkers as technologies intended to support reductions in premature cardiovascular mortality and describes connecting wearable and biosensor data to the NHS App and neighbourhood teams. This is policy direction rather than comparative effectiveness evidence. It supports the existence of a monitoring lever but not its numerical value or outcome multiplier.

title: 10 Year Health Plan, chapter 9: productivity and finance
text: Chapter 9 proposes year-of-care payments spanning primary, community, mental-health, outpatient, emergency and inpatient care, with pioneer work beginning in financial year 2026 to 2027. It states that implementation depends on reliable cost and activity data. This supports cross-service policy design and outcome-based incentives. It does not identify patient-flow probabilities and should not be used as a routing-share prior.

title: Community health services two-hour urgent community response standard
text: The national urgent community response standard is framed around a 2-hour response for eligible crisis-response referrals. The standard concerns elapsed time from referral to response, not the duration of the clinical visit. Do not map 120 minutes to community visit service time. It is an access standard and is useful for validating a waiting-time output or service-level constraint.

title: Two-hour urgent community response statistics
text: The published collection reports the percentage of urgent community response referrals receiving a response within 2 hours. The current national expectation is at least 70%. The publication warns that figures before and after the April 2023 definition change are not directly comparable. This is an observed service-level output, not a capacity multiplier.

title: Community Services Data Set technical guidance for the two-hour UCR standard
text: The technical definition measures whether an urgent community response begins within 120 minutes of the referral. It describes crisis-response intervention as short term, typically lasting up to 48 hours, and specifies the referral and response timestamps required for calculation. The 0-to-48-hour intervention window is a programme-duration boundary, not an individual visit duration. Preserve that context in retrieval.

title: Virtual wards operational framework
text: The framework expects virtual wards to maintain occupancy consistently above 80% while providing hospital-level care at home with defined clinical governance and escalation. The occupancy threshold is an operating target, not an effect size. It can validate utilisation outputs but must not be substituted for monitoring intensity or routing share.
